Sweep the handles together in a hugging arc to just in front of your chest. Squeeze for a moment.
Return over 2 to 3 seconds and let the cables pull your arms back into a full stretch before the next rep.
Avoid standing too far forward. If the cables lose tension at the start, the stretched part of the rep is wasted.
dumbbell: Lie on a flat bench with feet planted, shoulder blades pulled back and down, and a slight arch in your upper back.
Press the dumbbells over your chest with palms facing each other and a soft, fixed bend in the elbows.
Lower the weights out to the sides in a wide arc over 2 to 3 seconds until you feel a deep chest stretch.
Stop when your upper arms are about level with the bench or just below, as far as your shoulders allow comfortably.
Bring the dumbbells back up in the same arc, stopping a little short of touching where tension drops off.
Avoid going too heavy. The stretch at the bottom is the point, and heavy weights force you to bend the elbows and cut range.

Press up and slightly in until your arms are almost straight, keeping the shoulder blades on the pad.
Lower over 2 to 3 seconds until you feel a strong stretch in the upper chest, then press again.
Avoid letting the shoulders roll forward at lockout. It shifts the load to the front delts and loses the chest.

Avoid cutting the bottom short. The extra depth dumbbells allow is their main advantage over a barbell.

Avoid setting the bench too low on the rails. If the bar lands on your mid chest or neck, you lose the upper chest focus.

smith: Set the smith bar at about mid-thigh height and grip about shoulder width or wider.

Pull up, leading with the elbows, until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
Stay close to the bar so it runs straight up your body.
Avoid using a narrow grip. It increases shoulder strain without adding benefit.

s: Set the seat so your armpits rest snugly on the top of the pad and your upper arms lie flat on it.
Grip the handles with palms up and arms nearly straight.
Curl the handles toward your shoulders, keeping the upper arms on the pad.
Lower over 2 to 3 seconds until the arms are almost straight and the biceps feel stretched.
Push the last reps close to failure. The machine keeps form strict.
Avoid lifting your elbows off the pad. That lets the shoulders help and reduces biceps work.

machine: Set the seat so your armpits rest snugly on the top of the pad and your upper arms lie flat on it.

barbell: Set the preacher seat so your armpits sit on the top of the pad and the upper arms rest flat on it.
Grip an EZ bar or straight bar at about shoulder width with palms up.
Curl up until the forearms are near vertical.
Lower over 2 to 3 seconds until the arms are almost straight.
Keep the lowering slow. The bottom of a preacher curl is where the biceps are stretched and work hardest.
Avoid dropping into the bottom fast. Controlled lowering protects the elbows and builds the most muscle.
dumbbell: Set the preacher seat so your armpit sits on the top of the pad. Train one arm at a time.
Rest the upper arm flat on the pad and hold the dumbbell with your palm up.
Curl up until the forearm is near vertical.
Lower over 2 to 3 seconds until the arm is almost straight.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch.
Avoid lifting the elbow or shoulder off the pad. Keep the upper arm pinned.

s: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your sides.
Pin your elbows at your sides.
Curl the dumbbells up keeping the palms facing in. This trains the brachialis and forearm along with the biceps.
Stop when the forearms are near vertical, then lower over 2 to 3 seconds.
Straighten the arms fully at the bottom on every rep.
Avoid swinging the torso. Momentum takes the load off the target muscles.

Stop when the forearms are near vertical, then lower over 2 to 3 seconds.

cable: Set the pulley at the lowest position and attach a rope.
Hold the rope with palms facing each other and stand a step back from the stack.
Pin the elbows at your sides and curl the rope toward your shoulders.
Lower over 2 to 3 seconds until the arms are fully straight.
Keep tension on the cable at the bottom of each rep.
Avoid leaning back to lift more. Keep the torso upright.

s: Stand tall with feet hip width apart and grip the bar at about shoulder width, palms up.

Lower over 2 to 3 seconds until the arms are fully straight.
Allow only a slight forward move of the elbows at the top. Keep the rest of the body still.
Avoid swinging the hips to start the curl. If you need to, the weight is too heavy.

Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, keeping the elbows by your sides.
Lower over 2 to 3 seconds until the arms are fully straight.
Alternate arms or curl both at once.
Avoid swinging the torso. Keep the reps strict so the biceps do the work.

Squeeze at the top, then lower over 2 to 3 seconds to straight arms.

Pin the working elbow at your side with the forearm about parallel to the floor or higher.
Push the handle down until the arm is fully straight.
Return over 2 to 3 seconds until the elbow is fully bent and the triceps stretch.
